title: Change entry failed
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/work-items/changes/failed, application/json, with which an adapter reports that it stopped trying to post the comment of a comment entry of the change feed (changes.schema.json) on its item, or to put a repository of a submission entry on the forge. A report about a comment has comment_id, and a report about a repository of a submission has submission_id, system and path; a report has one of the two, never both. A report about a repository of a submission may have detail; a report about a comment has none. For a comment, the control plane marks that comment not posted and stores reason, and keeps the comment with the item's other comments. For a repository of a submission, it stores reason, and detail when it is set, with the submission version, so the work item's pages show that the commits of that repository have no address and that it has no draft. The adapter sends the report after a failure that trying again cannot fix. After a failure that trying again can fix, such as a timeout, a failed connection, a busy status or a 5xx status, it sends the report with reason unreachable, once its retries end. It sends one report for one comment entry, and none for a comment it posted. It sends one report for one repository of a submission entry, and none for a repository it put on the forge. The control plane checks permissions first, in the order of refusal.schema.json: it returns 403 forbidden for a request the access key has no permission for. The request has no connection_id and no collection_ref, so connection_unknown, connection_ended, connection_suspended and collection_not_linked do not apply to it. The control plane returns a signed 204 and changes nothing for a comment_id that is not the comment_id of a comment entry in the adapter's change feed. It does the same for the comment_id of a comment that it already matched to a posted comment (source-item-comments.schema.json, comment_id), and for a submission_id, system and path that are not those of a repository of a submission entry in the adapter's change feed, or whose repository the control plane already has a reply for (changes-submitted.schema.json). So a repeated or late report is never an error. On success the control plane returns a signed 204 with no body. The adapter acts on each answer as follows. On the signed 204, it does not send the report again. On 403 forbidden or 400 invalid_request, it stops sending the report. On a transient failure, no answer, a 5xx or an unsigned answer, it sends the report again, built anew as definitions.schema.json describes a retry, with backoff, and on a signed 429 it waits the seconds of Retry-After first. It stops sending the report once its retries of the report end, and logs the comment_id or the submission_id. The adapter logs each refusal with the comment_id or the submission_id, and never with the comment's or the draft's text, an access key or a secret. The request is signed with the adapter's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. Set time from the adapter's clock and sign each request anew: the control plane returns an unsigned 401 for a time more than 300 seconds off its clock, either way, and for a request whose signature it has already seen; definitions.schema.json has the replay rule. Send only the members this schema defines: the control plane returns 400 invalid_request for any other member.

version.description: The document format. Set it to 1: the control plane returns 400 invalid_request for any other version.

time.description: When the adapter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. Set it from the adapter's clock: the control plane returns an unsigned 401 for a time more than 300 seconds off its clock, either way.

comment_id.description: The comment_id of the comment entry whose comment the adapter stopped trying to post. Present exactly when submission_id is absent.

submission_id.description: The submission_id of the submission entry whose repository the adapter stopped trying to put on the forge. Present exactly when comment_id is absent, with system and path.

system.description: The system of the repository of the submission entry, as the entry has it. Present exactly with submission_id.

path.description: The path of the repository of the submission entry, as the entry has it. Present exactly with submission_id.

detail.description: The cause of the failure of a repository of a submission, one line of 1 to 1000 characters: first what to do about it, then the forge's status and message, such as "Shorten the title, then try again. The forge returned 422: title is too long." Optional with every reason of a submission. The adapter never puts an access token, a secret or a header in it. It has no control character, so no line break, no bidirectional control and none of the format characters that are usually not shown, the characters description.schema.json refuses in a line. A report about a comment has no detail: the control plane returns 400 invalid_request for it.

reason.description: Why the adapter stopped. For a comment: item_gone, not_permitted, too_long or unreachable. For a repository of a submission: not_permitted, unreachable, branch_gone, too_long or forge_refused.

Why the adapter stopped putting the repository on the forge: not_permitted, the forge returned that the integration's account has no permission to push to, read or open a draft in the repository; unreachable, each request to the forge timed out, failed to connect, or returned a busy status or a 5xx status, until the adapter's retries ended; branch_gone, the forge returned that the branch of the entry or its base branch does not exist, as after it was deleted; too_long, the title or the description is longer than the forge's limit for a draft; forge_refused, the forge refused a request with a status that no other reason covers, such as 400, or 422 for a cause other than a missing branch or a length limit, so the same request fails again.

Why the adapter stopped trying to post the comment: item_gone, the source returned that the item does not exist, as after it was deleted; not_permitted, the source returned that the integration's account has no permission to comment on the item; too_long, the comment with its first line is longer than the source's limit for a comment; unreachable, each request to the source timed out, failed to connect or returned a busy status, until the adapter's retries ended.
